results.title: Horn formula
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A CNF formula is a Horn formula when every clause contains at most one distinct positive literal.

results.title: Body of a clause contained in a set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite set $T$ of variables and a CNF clause $C$, this Boolean test is true exactly when every negative literal of $C$ has its variable in $T$.

results.title: Forward-chaining step
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$ and a finite set $T$ of variables, the derived set consists of the variables $x$ such that some clause of $\varphi$ contains the positive literal $x$ and has every one of its negative literals on a variable in $T$.

results.title: Forward-chaining closure
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$ and a finite set $T$ of variables, the closure of $T$ is computed by iterating the forward-chaining step of $\varphi$: if every variable derived from $T$ already lies in $T$, the closure is $T$; otherwise it is the closure of the union of $T$ with the derived variables.

results.title: Least model candidate
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, the least model candidate is the assignment that makes a variable true exactly when it lies in the forward-chaining closure of the empty set under $\varphi$.

results.title: On Horn formulas, the least model candidate lies below every model
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a Horn CNF formula and $\sigma$ an assignment satisfying $\varphi$. Every variable that the least model candidate of $\varphi$ makes true is also true under $\sigma$.

results.title: Horn satisfiability via the least model
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A Horn CNF formula $\varphi$ is satisfiable if and only if its least model candidate satisfies $\varphi$.

results.title: Horn satisfiability test
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, the Horn satisfiability test returns the Boolean truth value of $\varphi$ under its least model candidate.

results.title: Correctness of the Horn satisfiability test
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $\varphi$ is a Horn CNF formula, then the Horn satisfiability test returns true on $\varphi$ if and only if $\varphi$ is satisfiable.

results.title: 3-clause
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A 3-clause on $n$ variables is a pair $(S, p)$ of a three-element set $S$ of variables among the $n$ and a polarity $p$ assigning a Boolean value to every variable, with $p$ equal to false at every variable outside $S$. This normalization gives each clause in the usual sense (a three-element variable set with one of $2^3$ polarity patterns) exactly one representative.

results.title: Upper threshold cutoff
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A real number $\rho$ is an upper threshold cutoff for random 3-SAT when, for every real $r > \rho$, the probability that a uniformly random formula with $\lfloor r n \rfloor$ clauses on $n$ variables is satisfiable tends to $0$ as $n \to \infty$ (when $r n < 0$ the formula has no clauses); equivalently, such a formula is unsatisfiable with probability tending to $1$.

results.title: Lower threshold cutoff

results.title: Upper threshold of random 3-SAT

The infimum is taken to be $0$ when this set is empty or unbounded below.

results.title: Lower threshold of random 3-SAT
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The lower threshold is the supremum, in the real numbers, of the set of lower threshold cutoffs: the reals $\rho$ such that, for every real $r < \rho$, the probability that a uniformly random formula with $\lfloor rn \rfloor$ clauses on $n$ variables (no clauses when $rn < 0$) is satisfiable tends to $1$ as $n \to \infty$. The supremum is taken to be $0$ when this set is empty or unbounded above.

results.title: Random 3-SAT threshold conjecture
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: There is a real number $c$ that is both a lower and an upper threshold cutoff: for every real $r < c$, the probability that a uniformly random formula with $\lfloor r n \rfloor$ clauses on $n$ variables is satisfiable tends to $1$ as $n \to \infty$, and for every real $r > c$ this probability tends to $0$ (when $r n < 0$ the formula has no clauses).

results.title: Clauses as variable sets with polarity patterns
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For every $n$, the 3-clauses on $n$ variables correspond bijectively to the pairs $(S, q)$ of a three-element set $S$ of variables among the $n$ and a Boolean polarity $q$ on the variables of $S$: a clause is sent to its variable set together with its polarity restricted to that set.

results.title: CNF clause of a random 3-SAT clause
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The CNF clause of a clause $c$ on $n$ variables is the list of literals $(i, b_i)$, one for each of the three variables $i$ of $c$ taken as a natural-number index, where $b_i$ is the polarity that $c$ prescribes for $i$; the literals are listed in some fixed order.

results.title: Extension of an assignment by false
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An assignment $a$ of Boolean values to the variables $0, \dots, n - 1$ extends to all natural-number variables by giving variable $i$ the value $a(i)$ when $i < n$ and the value false otherwise.

results.title: Satisfying a clause through a restricted assignment
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ assign a Boolean value to every natural-number variable, and let $c$ be a 3-clause on the $n$ variables $0, \dots, n - 1$. Then the restriction of $A$ to these $n$ variables satisfies $c$ if and only if $A$ satisfies the CNF clause of $c$: the list with one literal $(i, p_i)$ for each of the three variables $i$ of $c$, where $p_i$ is the polarity that $c$ prescribes at $i$. A CNF clause is satisfied when…

results.title: CNF formula of a random 3-SAT formula
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The CNF formula of a formula $F$ with $m$ clauses $F_0, \dots, F_{m-1}$ on $n$ variables is the list of the CNF clauses of $F_0, \dots, F_{m-1}$, in this order.

results.title: Random 3-SAT satisfiability agrees with CNF satisfiability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A formula $F$ with $m$ clauses on $n$ variables is satisfiable if and only if its CNF formula, which lists each clause of $F$ as its three literals (variable index, polarity), is satisfiable as a CNF formula: some assignment of truth values to all natural-number variable indices makes at least one literal of every clause true.

results.title: Díaz–Kirousis–Mitsche–Pérez-Giménez upper bound for random 3-SAT
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The number $4.49$ is an upper threshold cutoff for random 3-SAT: for every real $r > 4.49$, the probability that a uniformly random formula with $\lfloor r n \rfloor$ clauses on $n$ variables is satisfiable tends to $0$ as $n \to \infty$.

results.title: Hajiaghayi–Sorkin lower bound for random 3-SAT
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The number $3.52$ is a lower threshold cutoff for random 3-SAT: for every real $r < 3.52$, the probability that a uniformly random formula with $\lfloor r n \rfloor$ clauses on $n$ variables (no clauses when $r < 0$) is satisfiable tends to $1$ as $n \to \infty$.

results.title: Erdős Problem 760: subgraphs of large cochromatic number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition asserts two statements. First, there is a real number $c > 0$ such that for every simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex set with chromatic number $m$ there are a subgraph $H$ of $G$ and a natural number $k$ with $k \ge c\,m / \log m$ such that the cochromatic number of $H$ is at least $k$. Second, there is a real number $c > 0$ with the same property for the bound $k \ge c\sqrt{m / \log m}$.

results.title: Alon–Krivelevich–Sudakov theorem on subgraphs of large cochromatic number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a real number $c > 0$ such that for every simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex set with chromatic number $m$ there are a subgraph $H$ of $G$ and a natural number $k$ with $k \ge c\,m / \log m$ such that the cochromatic number of $H$ is at least $k$. Moreover, there is a real number $c > 0$ with the same property for the bound $k \ge c\sqrt{m / \log m}$.

results.title: Kd-trees
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: A kd-tree over points of $\mathbb{Z}^d$ is either empty, a leaf holding one point of $\mathbb{Z}^d$, or a split node holding a split axis $a \in \{0, \dots, d-1\}$, a split value $s \in \mathbb{Z}$ and two kd-trees, its left and right subtrees.

results.title: Kd-tree point traversal with an accumulator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a kd-tree $t$ over points of $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and a list $\mathit{acc}$ of such points, the accumulator traversal of $t$ onto $\mathit{acc}$ is $\mathit{acc}$ when $t$ is empty, the point $p$ followed by $\mathit{acc}$ when $t$ is a leaf holding $p$, and, when $t$ is a split node with left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$, the traversal of $L$ onto the traversal of $R$ onto $\mathit{acc}$.

results.title: Point list of a kd-tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The point list of a kd-tree is the list of the points stored at its leaves, from left to right.

results.title: Accumulator traversal of a kd-tree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every kd-tree $t$ over $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and every list $acc$ of points, the accumulator traversal of $t$ onto $acc$ equals the list of points of $t$ in left-to-right order followed by $acc$.

results.title: Point list of a kd-tree split node
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a split node with axis $a$, split value $s$, left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$, the point list of the node is the point list of $L$ followed by the point list of $R$.

results.title: Size of a kd-tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The size of a kd-tree is defined by recursion: the empty tree has size $0$, a leaf has size $1$, and a split node has the sum of the sizes of its two children. Since points are stored only at leaves, this is the number of points stored in the tree, counted with multiplicity.

results.title: Length of the point list of a kd-tree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every kd-tree $t$, the list of the points stored in $t$, read from left to right, has length equal to the size of $t$, the number of points stored in $t$.

results.title: Next split axis of a kd-tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a dimension $d \ge 1$ and an axis $a \in \{0, \dots, d - 1\}$, the next split axis is $(a + 1) \bmod d$, so the axes are visited cyclically.

results.title: Membership in an axis-aligned box
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For $lo, hi, p \in \mathbb{Z}^d$, the point $p$ lies in the closed axis-aligned box $[lo, hi]$ when $lo_i \le p_i \le hi_i$ for every coordinate $i \in \{0, \dots, d-1\}$.

results.title: Accumulator range report of a kd-tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Points are vectors in $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with coordinates $p_0, \dots, p_{d-1}$; the box $[lo, hi]$ consists of the points $p$ with $lo_i \le p_i \le hi_i$ for every $i$. For a kd-tree $t$ and a list $acc$ of points, the accumulator report of $t$ for $[lo, hi]$ onto $acc$ is defined by recursion on $t$. For the empty tree it is $acc$. For a leaf $p$ it is $p$ followed by $acc$ if $p$ lies in the box, and $acc$…

results.title: Orthogonal range report of a kd-tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a kd-tree $t$ over $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and $lo, hi \in \mathbb{Z}^d$, the range report of $t$ for the box $[lo, hi]$ is the accumulator range report of $t$ for $[lo, hi]$ onto the empty list.

results.title: Kd invariant
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: A kd-tree satisfies the kd invariant when at every split node, with axis $a$ and split value $s$, every point of the left subtree has $a$-coordinate at most $s$ and every point of the right subtree has $a$-coordinate at least $s$.

results.title: Accumulator range report of a valid kd-tree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ be a valid kd-tree over $\mathbb{Z}^d$, let $lo, hi \in \mathbb{Z}^d$, and let $acc$ be a list of points. The accumulator range report of $t$ for the box $[lo, hi]$ onto $acc$ equals the list of points of $t$, in left-to-right order, that lie in the box (the points $p$ with $lo_i \le p_i \le hi_i$ for every coordinate $i$), followed by $acc$.

results.title: Correctness of the kd-tree range report
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every valid kd-tree $t$ over $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and all $lo, hi \in \mathbb{Z}^d$, the range report of $t$ for the box $[lo, hi]$ equals the list of points of $t$, in left-to-right order, that lie in the box, that is, the points $p$ with $lo_i \le p_i \le hi_i$ for every coordinate $i$.

results.title: Range report of a valid kd-tree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ be a kd-tree over $\mathbb{Z}^d$ that satisfies the kd invariant, and let $lo, hi, p \in \mathbb{Z}^d$. Then $p$ occurs in the range report of $t$ for the box $[lo, hi]$ if and only if $p$ is one of the points stored in $t$ and $lo_i \le p_i \le hi_i$ for every coordinate $i$.

results.title: First-point coordinate
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an axis $a \in \{0, \dots, d-1\}$ and a list of points in $\mathbb{Z}^d$, this is the $a$-coordinate of the first point of the list, or $0$ if the list is empty.

results.title: Median-split kd-trees satisfy the kd invariant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For $d \ge 1$, every axis $a$ and every list of points of $\mathbb{Z}^d$, the kd-tree built from the list by median splits starting at axis $a$ satisfies the kd invariant.

results.title: Building a kd-tree preserves its points
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For $d \ge 1$, every axis $a$ and every list of points of $\mathbb{Z}^d$, the point list of the kd-tree built from the list by median splits starting at axis $a$ is a permutation of the list.

results.title: A built kd-tree holds the same points as its input
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $d \ge 1$, let $a \in \{0, \dots, d-1\}$ and let $P$ be a list of points in $\mathbb{Z}^d$. A point $p \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ is stored in the kd-tree built from $P$ by median splits starting at axis $a$ if and only if $p$ occurs in $P$.

results.title: Size of a built kd-tree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $d \ge 1$. For every starting axis $a$ and every list $P$ of points of $\mathbb{Z}^d$, the size of the kd-tree built from $P$ starting at axis $a$ equals the length of $P$ (repeated points counted with multiplicity).

results.title: Kd-tree construction from the first axis
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $d \ge 1$ and a list of points in $\mathbb{Z}^d$, this is the kd-tree built from the list by alternating-axis median splits, starting with split axis $0$.

results.title: Kd-trees built from axis 0 satisfy the kd invariant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For $d \ge 1$ and every list of points of $\mathbb{Z}^d$, the kd-tree built from the list by median splits starting at axis $0$ satisfies the kd invariant.

results.title: Building a kd-tree from axis 0 preserves its points
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For $d \ge 1$ and every list of points of $\mathbb{Z}^d$, the point list of the kd-tree built from the list by median splits starting at axis $0$ is a permutation of the list.

results.title: Range report of a built kd-tree as a filter
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $d \ge 1$. For every starting axis $a$, every list $P$ of points of $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and all $lo, hi \in \mathbb{Z}^d$, let $T$ be the kd-tree built from $P$ starting at axis $a$. The range report of $T$ for the box $[lo, hi]$ equals the list of points of $T$, in left-to-right order, that lie in the box, that is, the points $p$ with $lo_i \le p_i \le hi_i$ for every coordinate $i$.

results.title: Range report of a built kd-tree up to order
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $d \ge 1$. For every starting axis $a$, every list $P$ of points of $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and all $lo, hi \in \mathbb{Z}^d$, the range report for the box $[lo, hi]$ of the kd-tree built from $P$ starting at axis $a$ is a permutation of the list of entries of $P$ that lie in the box, that is, the points $p$ with $lo_i \le p_i \le hi_i$ for every coordinate $i$.

results.title: Membership in the range report of a built kd-tree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $d \ge 1$, let $a \in \{0, \dots, d-1\}$, let $P$ be a list of points in $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and let $lo, hi, p \in \mathbb{Z}^d$. Then $p$ occurs in the range report, for the box $[lo, hi]$, of the kd-tree built from $P$ by median splits starting at axis $a$ if and only if $p$ occurs in $P$ and $lo_i \le p_i \le hi_i$ for every coordinate $i$.

results.title: Range report of a kd-tree built from the first axis
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $d \ge 1$, let $P$ be a list of points in $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and let $lo, hi, p \in \mathbb{Z}^d$. Then $p$ occurs in the range report, for the box $[lo, hi]$, of the kd-tree built from $P$ by median splits starting at axis $0$ if and only if $p$ occurs in $P$ and $lo_i \le p_i \le hi_i$ for every coordinate $i$.

results.title: Finite CCS processes
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: For a type $A$ of actions, the finite CCS processes over $A$ are built from the inactive process $\mathbf{0}$ by action prefix $a.P$ (an action $a \in A$ followed by a process $P$), nondeterministic choice $P + Q$, and parallel composition $P \mid Q$.

results.title: Operational semantics of finite CCS with a synchronization function
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a partial function that assigns to some pairs of actions $(a, b)$ an action $\sigma(a, b)$. The transition relation $P \xrightarrow{a} P'$ on finite CCS processes (built from prefix $a.P$, choice $P + Q$ and parallel composition $P \mid Q$) determined by $\sigma$ is the least relation such that $a.P \xrightarrow{a} P$; if $P \xrightarrow{a} P'$ then $P + Q \xrightarrow{a} P'$,…

results.title: Transitions of finite CCS without communication
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: The transition relation $P \xrightarrow{a} P'$ on finite CCS processes is the operational semantics of finite CCS whose synchronization function is undefined on every pair of actions. Thus prefix and choice move as usual, and a parallel composition $P \mid Q$ moves only by letting one of $P$ and $Q$ move; there are no communication steps.

results.title: Labelled transition system of finite CCS
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The labelled transition system whose states are the finite CCS processes, whose labels are the actions, and whose transitions $P \xrightarrow{a} P'$ are those of the communication-free operational semantics of finite CCS.

results.title: Lifting relations through choice
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: Given relations $R$ and $S$ on finite CCS processes, write $P_1 + P_2$ for the nondeterministic choice of $P_1$ and $P_2$. The choice lift of $R$ and $S$ relates $P$ to $Q$ exactly when $R(P, Q)$ holds, or $S(P, Q)$ holds, or $P = P_1 + P_2$ and $Q = Q_1 + Q_2$ with $R(P_1, Q_1)$ and $S(P_2, Q_2)$.

results.title: Prefix preserves strong bisimilarity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every action $a$ and all finite CCS processes $P$ and $Q$, if $P$ and $Q$ are strongly bisimilar in the labelled transition system of finite CCS, then the prefixed processes $a.P$ and $a.Q$ are strongly bisimilar there as well.

results.title: Reflexive closure of a relation on processes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a relation $E$ on finite CCS processes, its equation closure relates $P$ to $Q$ exactly when $P = Q$ or $E(P, Q)$; that is, it is the reflexive closure of $E$.

results.title: CCS labels
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: For a set of names, a CCS label is either the silent action $\tau$, the input on a name $a$, or the output on a name $a$.

results.title: Complementary labels
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Two CCS labels are complementary when one is the input on a name $a$ and the other is the output on the same name $a$, in either order. No other pair of labels is complementary; in particular the silent label $\tau$ has no complement.

results.title: Synchronization of CCS labels
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let the names form a type with decidable equality. For labels $a$ and $b$, the synchronization of $a$ with $b$ is the silent action $\tau$ when $a$ is the input on a name $n$ and $b$ is the output on the same name $n$, or when $a$ is the output on $n$ and $b$ is the input on $n$. For every other pair of labels, including any pair involving $\tau$, there is no result.

results.title: CCS transition relation with communication
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: The transition relation on CCS processes with labels over a set of names given by the raw step relation for the synchronization function under which an input and an output on the same name, in either order, synchronize to the silent label $\tau$, and no other pair of labels synchronizes.

results.title: Labelled transition system of CCS with communication
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The labelled transition system whose states are CCS processes with labels over a set of names, whose labels are CCS labels over those names, and whose transition relation is the CCS transition relation with communication.

results.title: Transitions of a parallel composition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For CCS processes $P$, $Q$, $R$ and a CCS label $a$, the parallel composition $P \mid Q$ has a transition labelled $a$ to $R$ in the CCS transition relation with communication if and only if one of the following holds: $P$ has a transition labelled $a$ to some $P'$ and $R = P' \mid Q$; or $Q$ has a transition labelled $a$ to some $Q'$ and $R = P \mid Q'$; or $a = \tau$ and there are processes $P'$, $Q'$ and…

results.title: Parallel lift of two relations
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: Given two relations $R$ and $S$ on CCS processes with labels over a set of names, their parallel lift relates a process $U$ to a process $V$ exactly when $R$ relates $U$ to $V$, or $S$ relates $U$ to $V$, or $U = P_1 \mid Q_1$ and $V = P_2 \mid Q_2$ where $R$ relates $P_1$ to $P_2$ and $S$ relates $Q_1$ to $Q_2$.

results.title: Parallel composition preserves strong bisimilarity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For CCS processes $P_1$, $P_2$, $Q_1$, $Q_2$ with labels over a set of names: if $P_1$ and $P_2$ are strongly bisimilar and $Q_1$ and $Q_2$ are strongly bisimilar in the labelled transition system of CCS with communication, then the parallel compositions $P_1 \mid Q_1$ and $P_2 \mid Q_2$ are strongly bisimilar there.

results.title: Prefix preserves strong bisimilarity in CCS with communication
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every CCS label $a$ and all CCS processes $P$ and $Q$: if $P$ and $Q$ are strongly bisimilar in the labelled transition system of CCS with communication, then so are the prefixed processes $a.P$ and $a.Q$.

results.title: Choice preserves strong bisimilarity in CCS with communication
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For CCS processes $P_1$, $P_2$, $Q_1$, $Q_2$ with labels over a set of names: if $P_1$ and $P_2$ are strongly bisimilar and $Q_1$ and $Q_2$ are strongly bisimilar in the labelled transition system of CCS with communication, then the choices $P_1 + Q_1$ and $P_2 + Q_2$ are strongly bisimilar there.

results.title: Parallel composition is commutative up to strong bisimilarity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all CCS processes $P$ and $Q$ with labels over a set of names, $P \mid Q$ and $Q \mid P$ are strongly bisimilar in the labelled transition system of CCS with communication.

results.title: The inactive process is a left unit for parallel composition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let the names form a type with decidable equality. For every CCS process $P$ over input, output and silent labels on these names, the parallel composition $0 \mid P$ of the inactive process $0$ with $P$ is strongly bisimilar to $P$ in the communication labelled transition system.

results.title: The inactive process is a right unit for parallel composition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let the names form a type with decidable equality. For every CCS process $P$ over input, output and silent labels on these names, the parallel composition $P \mid 0$ of $P$ with the inactive process $0$ is strongly bisimilar to $P$ in the communication labelled transition system.

results.title: Visible CCS label
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: A visible CCS label, excluding the silent action.

results.title: Complement of a visible label
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The complement of the input label on a channel $a$ is the output label on $a$, and the complement of the output label on $a$ is the input label on $a$.

results.title: Visible labels as CCS labels
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The inclusion of visible labels into CCS labels sends the input on a channel $a$ to the input on $a$, and the output on $a$ to the output on $a$.

results.title: Relabelling
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A finite CCS relabelling over channel names is a finite list of entries $(a, \ell)$, each pairing a channel name $a$ with a visible label $\ell$, that is, an input or an output on some channel. The entry $(a, \ell)$ gives $\ell$ as the image of the input on $a$; the image of the output on $a$ is then the complement of $\ell$. The first entry with name $a$ is used, and a name occurring in no entry is mapped to itself.

results.title: Applying a relabelling to a channel name
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $f$ be a finite relabelling whose table lists the entries $(a_1, \ell_1), \dots, (a_k, \ell_k)$, where each $a_i$ is a channel name and each $\ell_i$ a visible label. The image of a channel name $a$ under $f$ is $\ell_i$ for the first index $i$ with $a_i = a$, and the input label on $a$ when no entry has name $a$.

results.title: Static CCS processes
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: Finite CCS processes with the static operators, over a type of channel names, are built from the inactive process $0$ by the prefix $\alpha.P$ of a CCS action $\alpha$ (silent, an input or an output) and a process $P$, the choice $P + Q$, the parallel composition $P \mid Q$, the restriction $P \setminus L$ of $P$ by a finite list $L$ of names, and the relabelling $P[f]$ of $P$ by a finite relabelling $f$.

results.title: Embedding finite CCS into CCS with static operators
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Each finite CCS process over CCS labels is sent to the process with static operators of the same shape: the inactive process goes to the inactive process, the prefix of an action $\alpha$ to a process $P$ goes to the prefix of $\alpha$ to the image of $P$, and a choice or a parallel composition of $P$ and $Q$ goes to the choice or the parallel composition of the images of $P$ and $Q$.

results.title: Relabelling an action
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a relabelling $f$, the silent action $\tau$ is relabelled to $\tau$, an input on a channel $a$ is relabelled to the image of $a$ under $f$, and an output on $a$ is relabelled to the complement of the image of $a$ under $f$, each viewed as a CCS label.

results.title: Relabelling preserves complementary actions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every relabelling $f$ and all CCS labels $\alpha$ and $\beta$, if $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are complementary, then the actions obtained by relabelling $\alpha$ and $\beta$ with $f$ are complementary.

results.title: Actions permitted by a restriction
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a finite list $L$ of blocked channel names, the silent action $\tau$ is always permitted, and an input or an output on a channel $a$ is permitted exactly when $a \notin L$.

results.title: Transitions of static CCS
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: The labelled transition relation $P \xrightarrow{\alpha} P'$ on static CCS processes, with actions $\alpha$ the CCS labels (silent $\tau$, inputs and outputs), is the least relation closed under the following rules, where $\alpha.P$ is the prefix, $P + Q$ the choice, $P \mid Q$ the parallel composition, $P \setminus L$ the restriction of $P$ by a finite list $L$ of channel names, and $P[f]$ the relabelling of $P$…

results.title: Transition system of CCS with restriction and relabelling
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The labelled transition system of finite CCS with static operators has the finite CCS processes with restriction and relabelling as states and the CCS labels as labels, and its transitions are the steps of the structural operational semantics of these processes.

results.title: Lifting a relation through a restriction
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: Given a finite list $L$ of channel names and a relation $R$ on static CCS processes, the lifted relation relates $P$ to $Q$ exactly when either $R$ relates $P$ to $Q$, or $P = P' \setminus L$ and $Q = Q' \setminus L$ for some processes $P'$ and $Q'$ that $R$ relates.

results.title: Restriction preserves strong bisimilarity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite list $L$ of channel names and all static CCS processes $P$ and $Q$, if $P$ and $Q$ are strongly bisimilar in the labelled transition system of finite CCS with static operators, then so are the restricted processes $P \setminus L$ and $Q \setminus L$.

results.title: Closure of a relation under one relabelling
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: Given a relabelling $f$ and a relation $R$ on finite CCS processes with static operators, the lifted relation is the least relation that relates $P$ to $Q$ and relates the relabelling of $P$ by $f$ to the relabelling of $Q$ by $f$ whenever $R$ relates $P$ to $Q$.

results.title: Relabelling preserves strong bisimilarity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every relabelling $f$ and all finite CCS processes $P$ and $Q$ with static operators, if $P$ and $Q$ are strongly bisimilar in the labelled transition system of finite CCS with static operators, then the relabellings of $P$ and of $Q$ by $f$ are strongly bisimilar there.

results.title: Recursive CCS processes
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: Given a set of names and a set of process constants, the recursive CCS processes are generated by the following constructors: the inactive process $\mathbf{0}$; a process constant $A$; a prefix $\alpha.P$ for a CCS label $\alpha$ and a process $P$; a choice $P + Q$; a parallel composition $P \mid Q$; a restriction $P \setminus L$ for a finite list $L$ of names; and a relabelling $P[f]$ for a CCS relabelling $f$.

results.title: Recursive CCS specification
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: Given a type of channel names and a type of process constants, a recursive specification assigns to each process constant $A$ a defining body: a CCS process expression over those names, which may itself mention process constants (including $A$).

results.title: Transitions of recursive CCS
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: Let the channel names have decidable equality and let $\Delta$ be a recursive specification, assigning to each process constant $A$ its defining body $\Delta(A)$. The labelled transition relation $P \xrightarrow{\alpha} P'$ relative to $\Delta$ on recursive CCS processes, with actions $\alpha$ the CCS labels (silent $\tau$, inputs and outputs), is the least relation closed under the following rules, where…

results.title: Labelled transition system of a recursive specification
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Assuming equality of names is decidable, for a recursive specification $\Delta$ the labelled transition system generated by $\Delta$ has the recursive CCS processes as states and the CCS labels as labels, and its transitions $P \xrightarrow{\alpha} P'$ are exactly the steps of the structural operational semantics relative to $\Delta$.

results.title: Guardedness under a prefix flag
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a Boolean flag $b$, recording whether an action prefix has already been crossed, guardedness of a recursive CCS process under $b$ is defined recursively: the inactive process $\mathbf{0}$ is guarded under $b$; a constant $A$ is guarded under $b$ exactly when $b$ is true; a prefix $\alpha.Q$ is guarded under $b$ when $Q$ is guarded under true; a choice $Q + R$ or a parallel composition $Q \mid R$ is guarded…

results.title: Guarded process
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A recursive CCS process is guarded when all of its constant occurrences lie beneath an action prefix.

results.title: Every process is guarded beneath a prefix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every recursive CCS process $P$ is guarded under the flag $\mathrm{true}$: once an action prefix has been crossed, every constant occurrence counts as guarded.

results.title: Constant occurrences of a process
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The constant occurrences of a recursive CCS process $P$ are the list of the process constants occurring in $P$, from left to right and with repetitions: the inactive process $\mathbf{0}$ has none; a constant $A$ has the single occurrence $A$; a prefix $\alpha.Q$, a restriction $Q \setminus L$ and a relabelling $Q[f]$ have the occurrences of $Q$; and a choice $Q + R$ or a parallel composition $Q \mid R$ has the…

results.title: Constants of a process
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Assuming equality of process constants is decidable, the constants of a recursive CCS process $P$ are the list obtained from the constant occurrences of $P$ by removing duplicates, so that every process constant occurring in $P$ appears in it exactly once.

results.title: Renaming process constants
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a map $\rho$ from one set of process constants to another, renaming the constants of a recursive CCS process $P$ by $\rho$ replaces each occurrence of a constant $A$ by $\rho(A)$ and leaves $P$ otherwise unchanged: the inactive process, prefixes, choices, parallel compositions, restrictions and relabellings are kept as they are.

results.title: Renaming constants preserves guardedness
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $P$ be a recursive CCS process, let $\rho$ be a map from its process constants to another set of constants, and let $P\rho$ be the process obtained from $P$ by renaming its constants by $\rho$. Then for each Boolean flag $b$, $P\rho$ is guarded under $b$ if and only if $P$ is guarded under $b$.

results.title: Guarded recursive specification
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A recursive specification $\Delta$, which assigns to each process constant $A$ a body $\Delta(A)$, is guarded when for every constant $A$ the body $\Delta(A)$ is a guarded process.

results.title: Negative-binomial offspring probabilities
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The negative-binomial offspring probability with mean `R` and dispersion `k`: `P(Z = n) = C(k + n - 1, n) p^k (1 - p)^n` with `p = k / (k + R)` (Lloyd-Smith et al. 2005). Meaningful for `k > 0`, `R ≥ 0`.

results.title: Negative-binomial probability generating function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The negative-binomial generating function `G_k(s) = (1 + (R / k) (1 - s))^{-k}`.

results.title: Negative-binomial offspring distribution
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The negative-binomial offspring law as a measure on `ℕ`.

results.title: Nonnegativity of the negative-binomial probabilities
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The negative-binomial probabilities are nonnegative for `k > 0`, `R ≥ 0`.

results.title: Generating-function identity
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Negative-binomial offspring law is a probability measure
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The negative-binomial offspring law is a probability measure (`k > 0`, `R ≥ 0`).

results.title: Generating function of the negative-binomial law in closed form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The generating function of the negative-binomial offspring law is `nbPgf` on `[0, 1]`.

results.title: Monotonicity in the dispersion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `R ≥ 0`, `s ∈ [0, 1]` and `0 < k₁ ≤ k₂`, `G_{k₂}(s) ≤ G_{k₁}(s)`; equivalently `k ↦ k log (1 + x / k)` is nondecreasing for `x ≥ 0`.

results.title: Negative-binomial law with dispersion one is geometric
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `k = 1` is the geometric offspring law: `G_1(s) = 1 / (1 + R (1 - s))`.

results.title: Poisson limit
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: As `k → ∞`, `G_k(s) → e^{-R (1 - s)}` (for all real `R`, `s`).

results.title: Comparison principle for Galton–Watson extinction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If the offspring generating functions satisfy `f₂ ≤ f₁` on `[0, 1]`, then the extinction probabilities satisfy `q₂ ≤ q₁`.

results.title: Negative-binomial extinction probability is the least fixed point
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The extinction probability of the negative-binomial epidemic is the least fixed point of `G_k` in `[0, 1]`.

results.title: Superspreading raises the extinction probability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Superspreading raises the extinction probability (Lloyd-Smith et al. 2005): at a fixed mean `R ≥ 0`, the probability `q_k` that the outbreak started by one case goes extinct is nonincreasing in the dispersion `k > 0`.
